mainTopic: Tearing a bird עולה by hand, and why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows separating the head of a חטאת העוף
overview: The גמרא explains several lines of the משנה about bird offerings. First, a ברייתא proves from the פסוק about שמשון that the 'tearing' (שיסוע) of a bird עולה is done by hand. Next, the גמרא notes that the משנה, which says separating the head of a חטאת העוף makes it פסול, does not follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who heard that one may separate it. Three אמוראים explain what they really argue about. רב חסדא says it is whether squeezing the blood (מיצוי) is essential. רבא says it is whether pausing (שהייה) at the second סימן ruins an עולת העוף. אביי says it is whether cutting most of the flesh (רוב בשר) is essential. The גמרא adds that רבא's and אביי's explanations match an earlier argument between רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק. It also proves from a ברייתא that רוב בשר is cut from the start. Finally, רבי ירמיה quotes a fuller tradition in which רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון goes on to explain the פסוק 'לא יבדיל', and that explanation comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Tearing the bird is done by hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'he tore and did not separate' and brings a ברייתא showing that 'tearing' (שיסוע) means tearing by hand, proven from the פסוק about שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the כהן 'tore the bird but did not separate it.' The חכמים taught in a ברייתא: the תורה says 'and he shall tear.' Tearing always means by hand, like the פסוק says about שמשון: 'and he tore it as one tears a young goat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a phrase from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains how the tearing is done: with the hands, not with a knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שיסוע in the פסוק about the bird עולה is unclear on its own. The ברייתא compares it to the same word used for שמשון tearing the lion, where the פסוק stresses he had nothing in his hand. So שיסוע means tearing with bare hands.

phrases.english: He tore and did not separate.
The Rabbis taught: "And he shall tear" —
tearing is only by hand,
and so it says:
"And he tore it as one tears a young goat."
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:6, about שמשון and the lion. The rest of that פסוק says he had nothing in his hand, which is the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by explaining a phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שיסוע of a bird עולה is done by hand, learned from וישסעהו כשסע הגדי.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and points out that its ruling (separating the head of a חטאת העוף makes it פסול) disagrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who heard that one may separate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'he did not remove the crop, etc.' Our משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. A ברייתא teaches that he said: 'I heard that one may separate the head in a חטאת העוף.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies a disagreement: the משנה says separating the head of a bird חטאת ruins it, but רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists things that do not ruin the bird offering, but rules that fully separating the head of a חטאת העוף makes it פסול. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reports a tradition that separating is allowed. This sets up the question of what exactly they argue about.

phrases.english: He did not remove the crop, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה. The part the גמרא cares about comes later there: separating the head of a חטאת העוף makes it פסול.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon;
as it was taught in a Baraita:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
I heard that one may separate in a bird sin offering.
phrases.notes: He means separating the head completely from the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה and identifies whose opinion it follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה (separating the head of a חטאת העוף makes it פסול) disagrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who allows separating.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying issue causes the משנה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון to disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: what is the real reason behind this disagreement?
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to know that they disagree; the גמרא wants the principle that drives each side. The answer will come from רב חסדא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point they differ on?

phrases.english: What is between them?
phrases.notes: He means: what is the underlying issue they argue about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the disagreement stated in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides the משנה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב חסדא: they argue whether squeezing the blood is essential
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the disagreement is about whether מיצוי (squeezing out the blood) of a חטאת העוף is essential. The תנא קמא holds it is, so separating the head plus squeezing the blood makes it look like an עולה procedure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: they differ about whether squeezing out the blood of a חטאת העוף is essential. The first תנא holds it is essential. So since the כהן must squeeze out the blood, if he also separates the head he is doing the procedure of an עולה on a חטאת העוף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question and explains the משנה's side: because squeezing the blood is required, separating the head would turn the procedure into an עולה procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird עולה has its head separated and its blood squeezed out. If מיצוי is essential for a חטאת העוף too, the כהן will always squeeze; adding a full separation makes the whole procedure match an עולה. Doing an עולה procedure on a חטאת is what makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Essential; without it the offering is not valid

steps.confusionAlert: Separating the head alone is not the problem for the תנא קמא. The problem is the combination: separating plus the required squeezing makes the procedure look like an עולה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
whether squeezing out a bird sin offering is essential —
that is the difference between them.
The first Tanna holds:
squeezing out a bird sin offering is essential;
and since he squeezes out the blood,
he is doing the procedure of a burnt offering on a bird sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מִיצּוּי חַטַּאת הָעוֹף מְעַכֵּב אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 and explains the משנה's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is whether מיצוי of a חטאת העוף is essential; the תנא קמא says yes, so separating plus squeezing equals an עולה procedure, making it פסול.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: squeezing is not essential
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains the other side: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds מיצוי is not essential, so separating the head is just cutting meat and does not ruin the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that squeezing out the blood of a חטאת העוף is not essential, so separating the head is just cutting meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his answer by explaining why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows separating the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since squeezing is not required, the כהן can separate the head and simply not squeeze. Without the squeezing, the procedure does not match an עולה, so the separation counts as ordinary cutting of meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Not essential; the offering is valid without it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that doing an עולה procedure on a חטאת העוף ruins it. They argue only about whether squeezing the blood is required: if yes (משנה), separating leads to an עולה procedure and is פסול; if no (רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון), separating is just cutting meat.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds:
squeezing out a bird sin offering is not essential,
and he is merely cutting meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's answer with the opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds מיצוי is not essential, so separating the head is mere cutting of meat and the offering stays valid.

steps.title: רבא's explanation: pausing before the second cut, and the first Tanna's side
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason for the disagreement: whether שהייה at the second סימן ruins an עולת העוף. The תנא קמא says it does not, so even after pausing, separating the head counts as doing an עולה procedure on a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is whether pausing at the second סימן of a bird עולה makes it פסול. The תנא קמא holds that pausing at the second סימן of a bird עולה does not make it פסול. So even if the כהן paused, when he separates the head he is doing an עולה procedure on a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new way to explain the argument in the משנה, different from רב חסדא's. He starts with the side of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא moves the argument away from מיצוי and onto שהייה, pausing in the middle of the pinching. If pausing does not ruin an עולת העוף, then a separated head still looks like a real עולה procedure, even with a pause. That is why the תנא קמא says the חטאת is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Pausing or stopping in the middle of the cutting
The second of the two organs (windpipe and food pipe) that are cut
A bird brought as an עולה
Holds back the offering, so it is not valid
This is the difference between them
Doing an עולה procedure on a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: The question of whether pausing ruins the offering is asked about an עולת העוף, but it is being used to decide a case of a חטאת העוף. The point is whether separating the head of the חטאת still counts as a real עולה procedure.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Pausing at the second siman
phrases.notes: The two סימנים are the windpipe and the food pipe. Pausing here means stopping before cutting the second one.

phrases.english: of a bird burnt offering disqualifies
is the difference between them.
The first Tanna holds:
pausing at the second siman of a bird burnt offering
does not disqualify;
and even though he paused,
phrases.notes: Now he is talking about the חטאת העוף whose head was separated.

phrases.english: he is doing a burnt-offering procedure on a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שְׁהִיָּיה בְּסִימָן שֵׁנִי בְּעוֹלַת הָעוֹף מְעַכֵּב אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 3, instead of רב חסדא's מיצוי explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement depends on whether שהייה at the second סימן ruins an עולת העוף. The תנא קמא says it does not, so separating the head of a חטאת is still an עולה procedure and makes it פסול.

steps.title: רבא's explanation: רבי אלעזר's side
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that שהייה does ruin an עולת העוף. So once the כהן paused, separating the head is not an עולה procedure. It is just cutting meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that pausing does make it פסול. So since he paused, he is just cutting meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by showing how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's side works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pausing ruins an עולה, then a head separated after a pause is not a real עולה procedure. So nothing in it counts as an "עולה act" done on the חטאת. It is just plain cutting of meat, and the חטאת stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting meat, an act that has no meaning for the offering

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds:
it disqualifies;
phrases.notes: He means that pausing ruins an עולת העוף.

phrases.english: and since he paused,
he is merely cutting flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation by giving the other side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that pausing ruins an עולה. So separating the head after a pause is just cutting meat, and the חטאת is not ruined.

steps.title: אביי's explanation: is cutting most of the flesh required
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a third explanation. The disagreement is about whether cutting רוב בשר (most of the flesh) is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The difference between them is whether cutting most of the flesh is required.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a third way to explain the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of מיצוי (רב חסדא) or שהייה (רבא), אביי says the question is whether cutting רוב בשר is necessary. The גמרא only names the issue here. It does not spell out how each side follows from it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
whether the majority of the flesh is indispensable
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: רוֹב בָּשָׂר מְעַכֵּב אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement depends on whether cutting רוב בשר is required.

steps.title: The same two explanations were argued by רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's and אביי's explanations match an earlier argument between רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק. One gave the שהייה explanation, and the other gave the רוב בשר explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the same as the argument of רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק. One said the difference is whether pausing at the second סימן of a bird עולה makes it פסול. The other said the difference is whether cutting most of the flesh is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by pointing out that these same two explanations were already argued by two earlier אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added about the law here. The גמרא is showing that the argument between רבא and אביי is the same as an earlier argument. The words חד אמר and וחד אמר tell us we are not told which אמורא held which view.

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and one said (without telling us who said which)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of the משנה's argument. רב חסדא says it is about מיצוי. רבא says it is about שהייה in an עולת העוף. אביי says it is about רוב בשר. The last two match the argument of רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק.

phrases.english: And this is in the dispute of Rabbi Zeira
and Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak;
one said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁהִיָּיה בְּסִימָן שֵׁנִי בְּעוֹלַת הָעוֹף מְעַכֵּב
phrases.english: whether pausing at the second siman of a bird burnt offering disqualifies
is the difference between them,
and one said:
whether the majority of the flesh is indispensable is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the explanations of רבא and אביי to an earlier argument between two other אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement between רבא and אביי is the same as the argument between רבי זירא and רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק.

steps.title: Does everyone agree that most of the flesh must be cut from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether אביי's explanation implies that everyone requires cutting רוב בשר from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we infer from this that we require cutting most of the flesh from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from אביי's explanation and asks whether it is really true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the argument is about whether רוב בשר is required. That suggests the argument is only about whether it is essential, meaning whether leaving it out ruins the offering. So the גמרא asks: does that mean everyone agrees the כהן should cut רוב בשר from the very start?

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; from this we can learn
Most of the flesh of the neck
From the start; the proper way to do it in the first place

phrases.english: Can we infer from this that we require
cutting most of the flesh from the start?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from אביי's רוב בשר explanation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether cutting רוב בשר is required from the start according to everyone

steps.title: Yes, and a ברייתא shows how מליקה is done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and brings a ברייתא showing that the כהן cuts רוב בשר together with the סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. And so it was taught in a ברייתא: How does one do מליקה on a bird sin offering? He cuts the spine and the back of the neck, without cutting most of the flesh, until he reaches the gullet or the windpipe. Once he reaches the gullet or the windpipe, he cuts one סימן or most of it, and most of the flesh along with it. And for a bird burnt offering, he cuts two סימנים or most of two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says yes, everyone agrees that רוב בשר is cut from the start, and it proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the proper way to do מליקה. The כהן goes through the spine and the back of the neck first, without cutting most of the flesh. When he cuts the סימן, he cuts רוב בשר along with it. So cutting רוב בשר is part of the proper procedure from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing מליקה: killing a bird offering by cutting from the back of the neck with the thumbnail
The spine and the back of the neck
One of the two signs of a valid slaughter, the gullet or the windpipe

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different moments of cutting flesh here. On the way through the spine he does NOT cut most of the flesh. When he cuts the סימן, he DOES cut most of the flesh along with it.

phrases.english: Yes; and so it was taught in a ברייתא:
How does one do מליקה on a bird sin offering?
He cuts the spine and the back of the neck
without cutting most of the flesh,
until he reaches the gullet or the windpipe.
Once he reached the gullet or the windpipe,
he cuts one סימן, or most of it,
and most of the flesh along with it.
And for a burnt offering: two, or most of two.
phrases.notes: He means two סימנים: both the gullet and the windpipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 and supports the answer with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That רוב בשר is cut from the start in מליקה of a חטאת העוף
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing how מליקה of a חטאת העוף is done

steps.title: רבי ירמיה cites a tradition that the head may be separated
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה hears the explanations and objects. He cites a tradition that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון held one separates the head of a חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said this before רבי ירמיה. He said: Have they not heard what רבי שמעון בן אליקים said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן פדת, in the name of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע? רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון used to say: I heard that for a bird sin offering, one separates the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The explanations of the argument (רב חסדא, רבא, אביי) are told to רבי ירמיה. He objects by quoting a tradition about what רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון really held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier explanation gave a technical reason why separating the head would not ruin the offering according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רבי ירמיה says they missed a fuller version of his tradition. That version does not stop at 'one separates.' It goes on to deal with the פסוק 'לא יבדיל' (next step), so his view seems to come from how he reads the פסוק, not from those technical points.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him; in front of him
One separates the head completely from the body

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge changes the direction of the סוגיא. Instead of looking for technical reasons, the גמרא must now explain how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's tradition fits with the פסוק.

phrases.english: They said this before רבי ירמיה,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the explanations the אמוראים gave for why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows separating the head.

phrases.english: he said: Have they not heard

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים
phrases.english: that which רבי שמעון בן אליקים said
in the name of רבי אלעזר בן פדת,
in the name of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון used to say:
I heard that for a bird sin offering, one separates the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, אָמַר: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges all the earlier explanations of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of רב חסדא, רבא and אביי for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's position
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fuller tradition of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's statement goes on to explain the פסוק 'לא יבדיל', which shows his view rests on reading the פסוק, not on the technical points the אמוראים proposed.

steps.title: What does 'he shall not separate' mean then?
steps.stepSummary: Within the tradition רבי ירמיה quotes, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון asks how the פסוק 'לא יבדיל' fits with his view that one separates the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'he shall not separate'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. It is still part of the tradition רבי ירמיה is quoting: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון himself asks what 'לא יבדיל' means, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says about the חטאת העוף 'ולא יבדיל', which means he shall not separate. If רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says one separates the head, he must read this פסוק in a different way. His explanation comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not separate (the head from the body)

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'he shall not separate'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the tradition quoted by רבי ירמיה: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון introduces his reading of 'לא יבדיל', which is the basis of רבי ירמיה's objection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads the פסוק 'לא יבדיל' if he holds that one separates the head
